page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is an enterprise-grade general-purpose virtual machine configuration engineered for massive multi-threaded scale and heavy computational density. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity reaches 720.0 GB of system RAM, allocating 3.75 GB per virtual core alongside a substantial 260 MB L3 cache pool and advanced instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX.

Benchmark evaluations position the c4-standard-192 in the top tier for multi-threaded processing. In stress-ng multi-core testing, it recorded an aggregate score of 165,332.95, supplemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,711.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 115,368.08. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth exceeds 577 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput memory channels. In practical throughput workloads, the system sustained over 212 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 227.94 GB/sec in static web serving metrics.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of integrated local storage and hardware GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on attached network volumes for persistent data. While single-thread benchmarks place in the average to strong categories, the sheer core count yields high computational efficiency for parallelized processing without the premium associated with specialized accelerator nodes. The platform provides strong CPU-based machine learning inference, registering 44.38 tokens per second on medium 7B parameter models.

Given its high core concentration, wide memory bandwidth, and substantial RAM pool, the c4-standard-192 is suited for large-scale enterprise databases, extensive software compilation toolchains, high-concurrency web microservices, and distributed data processing frameworks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a high-density general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 192 dedicated vCPUs (96 physical cores) based on the Intel Xeon 8581C processor at 2.3 GHz, supported by 720.0 GB of RAM and 260 MB of L3 cache. Featuring hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector acceleration, the instance delivers top-tier parallel execution benchmarks, including a PassMark CPU score of 115,368.08 and Redis throughput surpassing 212 million operations per second. It includes no local disk storage or hardware GPUs, focusing resource density entirely on CPU and system memory concurrency. This architecture represents a cost-efficient deployment profile for highly parallel software builds, large in-memory databases, and high-concurrency web serving environments.
